transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm in the right place. I'm just here because... well, I've been having a little trouble at home lately. 

It's probably nothing major, but I find myself spending... gosh, I guess most of my day just going back over things in the house. Like, checking the outlets, the locks, my tools... even just the dust. I just keep checking and fixing them again and again. I try to stop, but I end up doing it until I'm just completely worn out, and even then, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. 

I know it sounds a bit ridiculous, and I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well. Is that... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks in a specific way or order?

Um, yes, I guess I do. I hope that doesn't sound too strange... but like I was saying before about going back over the same outlets and the locks, and my tools and the dust? I do kind of have a set way I have to do it. 

If it doesn't feel right, I just have to fix it and check it all over again. I end up doing it again and again until I'm just completely worn out. And even after all that exhausting checking, I still don't really feel sure enough to just walk away and leave it alone. 

I try my best to keep it under control, really I do, it's just... maybe a little habit that got out of hand, I suppose. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Um, well... yes. I hope you don't think I'm losing my mind or anything when I say this, but... yeah. 

Even when I know for an absolute fact that I did a job right, these... I guess you could call them ugly thoughts, they just keep jumping into my head. Like, I'll suddenly start thinking that maybe there's a loose wire I missed somewhere, and it's going to spark and burn the whole house down. Or... or that I left a stray nail on the floor, and my wife is going to step on it and get really hurt. 

I try so hard to just push them out and focus on whatever else I'm doing, I really do. But it's like... the harder I try to ignore them, they just come right back, and usually even stronger. I know it's probably just my imagination running away with me, and I feel terrible even having thoughts like that. Is that... do other people get thoughts like that? Am I explaining it okay?
Do you feel like it's your responsibility to prevent these bad things from happening, like the house burning down or your wife getting hurt?

Well, I mean... I suppose so, yes. I hope that doesn't make me sound like some kind of control freak or anything. It's just... I'm the man of the house, you know? It's my job to make sure things are safe. 

I just want to be a good husband, and make sure she's okay. If I know there's a chance something could go wrong, and I don't do everything I can to check it and fix it... well, then it would be my fault if she got hurt, wouldn't it? I just couldn't live with myself if something happened to her because I was careless. 

I know it's probably normal for guys to worry about their families, right? I just... I might take it a little too far sometimes, that's all. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. Am I making sense?
Are these checking habits and thoughts interfering with your daily life, relationships, or work in any way?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I hope it doesn't make me sound lazy or anything, because I really do like to work, I promise. But... I actually had to stop taking paid carpentry jobs for right now. And I kind of pulled back from the community projects I used to help out with, too. 

It's just that... well, making sure the house is perfectly safe, it sort of ends up taking over my whole day. I get stuck there doing my checks, and I just end up so completely exhausted by the end of it. So my wife... she's been having to handle a lot more of the errands and the daily decisions lately. 

I feel terrible putting all that extra weight on her, I really do. I'm sure it's just a temporary thing until I get this little habit under control, you know? I want to get back to being the provider and pulling my weight. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
What happens if you're unable to perform your checks, do you feel anxious or uneasy?

Um, well... yeah. I do get a bit worked up, I suppose. I hope that doesn't make me sound too high-strung. I really try not to let it get to me, but... if I can't do my checks, it's just... it's really hard. 

Actually, that's kind of the main reason I came in to see you. I just... I spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, checking the locks, making sure my tools are put away perfectly, even checking for dust. I just keep checking and fixing them, over and over, until I'm just completely worn out. And even then, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit that I spend so much time on it. I know it probably sounds silly to worry so much about an outlet or a lock. I'm really hoping you can help me find a way to just... feel okay about it so I don't have to check so much. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you feel like you have to think certain thoughts or repeat certain words or phrases to yourself as part of your checking routine?

Um... no, I don't think so. I hope I'm not misunderstanding your question, I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. But... I don't really say any special words or phrases to myself. 

Like I was just saying a second ago, it's really just the physical actions for me. Going back over the outlets, making sure the locks are secure, checking the tools and the dust... just doing all that over and over. I just have to keep physically checking and fixing those same things until I'm completely worn out, rather than repeating any thoughts, you know? And even after all that checking, I still just never feel sure enough to leave it alone. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have any specific words I say. I don't want you to think I'm holding anything back. Does that... does that still make sense for what we're talking about? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
How much distress do these repeating thoughts cause you?

Um, well... I guess they do bother me a fair bit. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything, because I know people deal with much worse things. But... it is pretty stressful. 

It's just... even when I know, I *know* I did the job right, these... these ugly thoughts just keep jumping into my head. Like, I'll start thinking that a loose wire I missed is going to spark and burn the whole house down, or... or that a nail I left somewhere is going to hurt my wife. And I really try to just push those thoughts away and focus on something else, I promise I do. But they just... they come right back, and they feel even stronger. 

It makes me feel awful, honestly. Like I'm a bad person for even having those thoughts in the first place. I hope you don't think less of me for saying that. I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have these habits and thoughts affected your relationship with your wife in any significant way?

Um, well... I mean, she's been really wonderful about it. I hope I don't make it sound like she's complaining, because she's so patient with me. But... I guess it has changed things a bit between us. 

I actually... um, I stopped taking paid carpentry jobs a while ago. And I had to pull back from the community projects I used to help with, too. It's just... I want to be helpful, I really do, but doing all those checks around the house just kind of takes over my whole day. By the time I'm done, I'm just so exhausted. 

Because I get so stuck doing all that, my wife has had to take on a lot more. She handles most of the errands now, and she ends up having to make a lot of the decisions because I'm just... I'm tied up with the checking. I feel terrible putting that on her. I really want to be a good husband and do my fair share. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful... I'm really trying to get better so I can help her more. Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you feel like your checking habits are aimed at preventing something bad from happening to yourself or others?

Um, yes... I think so. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

But like I was saying earlier, that's really why I'm here talking to you today. I end up spending most of my day just... going back over the same outlets, the locks, my tools, the dust in the house... just checking and fixing them again and again. And I do it because I feel like I absolutely have to, to keep those bad things from happening. I just keep going until I'm completely worn out. But the hard part is, even then... I still just don't feel sure enough to leave it alone. 

I know it probably sounds silly that I can't just stop, and I really try to, I promise. I just want to keep my wife and our home safe, and I get so scared that if I don't check, it'll be my fault if something goes wrong. Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm explaining it okay, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy time with your wife or engage in activities you used to like because of your checking habits?

Um, well... I know I touched on this a little bit before, and I hope it's okay that I'm bringing it up again. I just want to make sure I'm answering you fully. 

But yes, it... it has made things harder to enjoy. Like I mentioned, I actually stopped taking paid carpentry jobs a while ago, and I had to step back from the community projects I used to love doing. I don't want you to think I'm lazy or anything—I really do want to work and help out. It's just... doing all the checks around the house, making sure everything is perfectly safe... it kind of takes over my whole day. 

And by the time I'm done, I'm just so completely exhausted that I don't have the energy for much else. It makes me feel terrible because, like I said, my wife has had to take on so much more. She handles the errands and makes a lot of the decisions because I just get so stuck checking everything. I really hate that I'm not doing my fair share, and I want to be a better partner to her. I hope I don't sound like I'm just making excuses. I'm really trying my best to get a handle on this so we can do fun things together again. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to be sure I'm being helpful.
Do you feel like you have to think about certain things or mentally replay certain events as part of your daily routine?

Um, well... I mean, I try not to. I don't want to have those kinds of thoughts, I really don't. I hope you don't think I'm crazy or something for saying this, but... yes, I do get these thoughts stuck in my head. 

It's like... even when I know, I absolutely know, that I did a job right, these really ugly thoughts just keep jumping into my mind. Like, I'll start thinking that maybe there's a loose wire I missed and it's going to burn the house down. Or... or that I left a nail somewhere and my wife is going to step on it and get hurt. And I know it sounds ridiculous, and I try so hard to just push the thoughts away and focus on other things. But... they just come right back, and they feel even stronger. 

I really try to keep my mind on positive things, I promise. It's just hard when my brain keeps telling me something terrible is going to happen because of something I did. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
Do you feel like your checking habits help reduce your anxiety about potential dangers?

Um... well, yes, I suppose they do help, just for a little bit. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer. 

But like I was saying before... the reason I'm here is because I spend most of my day just... going back over the same things. The outlets, the locks, my tools, even the dust in the house... I just keep checking and fixing them again and again. And when I do it, it... it does make that terrible scared feeling go away for a second. It makes me feel like I'm being responsible and keeping everything safe. 

But then... I don't know, it just doesn't last. I keep going until I'm completely worn out, but even then, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. I really don't want you to think I'm doing it just to be difficult or obsessive. I'm really trying to stop, I promise. It's just that the anxiety comes right back, and I feel like I have to do it all over again to make sure I didn't miss anything. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm making sense.
Do you feel like you have to follow a strict routine or set of rules in your daily life?

Um, well... I guess I do have sort of a routine, but I really hope it doesn't sound too strange or rigid. I don't mean to be difficult or anything, I just... I like to be thorough, you know? 

Like I was saying earlier, I spend a lot of my day going back over the same things—the outlets, the locks, making sure my tools are put away just right, checking the dust... I just keep checking and fixing them again and again. I guess that's my routine. I don't do it to be stubborn, I promise. It's just that I feel like I have to keep doing it until I'm completely worn out. And even then, I still don't feel sure enough to just leave it alone. 

I really try to just let things be, but it's like I have this set of rules in my head about how everything needs to be perfectly safe before I can stop. I hope that doesn't make me sound too... unhinged. I'm really trying to work on it. Is that the kind of routine you meant? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like your checking habits and thoughts are significantly interfering with your ability to enjoy life or function normally?

Um... well, I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or... or making excuses. I want to be productive, I promise I do. But... yeah, I guess it has been getting in the way a bit. 

I actually... I stopped taking on paid carpentry jobs recently. And I had to pull back from the community projects I used to help out with, too. It's just that keeping the house safe and going through my routine... it kind of takes over my whole day now. I don't mean for it to, but I get so stuck checking things that I just end up completely exhausted. 

My wife has had to start handling a lot more of the errands and the decisions for us because I just... I can't always get away from the house to help her. I feel terrible about it, I really do, and I'm trying so hard to fix it so I can be a better husband and get back to work. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful or useless. Is... is that what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
